t: Kyiv was the capital of Kievan Rus' from the late 9th century, reached its height in the middle of the 11th century under Yaroslav the Wise, and was left in ruins by the Mongols on 6 December 1240.
For centuries afterwards it was a provincial city under the Golden Horde, Lithuania, Poland and Russia, yet it remained the seat of the Orthodox metropolitan and a centre of Ukrainian culture.

It became the capital of short-lived Ukrainian states in 1917, of Soviet Ukraine in 1934 and of independent Ukraine in 1991, and it suffered greatly in the famine of 1932 and 1933 and in the Second World War.
dyk: Between 1146 and 1246 Kyiv changed hands 47 times and was ruled by 24 princes, 35 of whose tenures lasted less than a year.
ev: The traditional date of the city's founding, celebrated as its 1,500th anniversary in 1982
Prince Volodymyr I accepts Christianity and orders the people of Kyiv to be baptised in the Dnieper
An army of eleven princes sent by Andrei Bogolyubsky sacks the city for three days
Batu Khan's Mongols besiege Kyiv and destroy it
After the Battle of Blue Waters Kyiv passes to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania
The Truce of Andrusovo cedes Kyiv to the Tsardom of Russia
Nazi Germany occupies the city, and nearly 34,000 Jews are killed at Babi Yar
Ukraine declares independence in Kyiv, which becomes the capital of an independent state

f.founded: The date is debated: 482 CE is the traditional date, archaeological data indicates the 6th or 7th century, and some researchers date the founding as late as the late 9th century. According to the Primary Chronicle the brothers Kyi, Shchek and Khoryv and their sister Lybid founded it.
f.where: On both banks of the Dnieper River in north-central Ukraine, on the hills of the western bank, close to the mouth of the Desna.
f.known: Capital of Kievan Rus'; the baptism of 988; St Sophia Cathedral and the Monastery of the Caves; the Mongol destruction of 1240; the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy; capital of Soviet and then independent Ukraine; Babi Yar
f.today: Kyiv is the capital and most populous city of Ukraine, a city with the legal status of a region.
